summary: Preserves channel shape and sample rate while stretching or compressing samples into a new interval, with optional reverse playback.
key_concepts: Stretch CHOP preserves channel shape and sampling rate while resampling data into a new interval.
All data in the selected range is stretched or compressed to the new start and end positions.
Interpolation controls how values are reconstructed when interval length changes.
Pulse Preserve is intended to keep single-sample pulses at their height and one-sample width.
Constant Area scales values so the area under the channel stays constant.
Reverse Interval reverses the sample order of each channel after interval handling.

key_params.name: interp
key_params.note: No interpolation, linear, cubic, pulse preserve, or repeat samples

key_params.name: constarea
key_params.note: Preserve area under the channel by scaling values

key_params.name: relative
key_params.note: Absolute, relative to start/end, or relative to current frame

key_params.name: abs
key_params.note: Interpret start/end as new absolute positions

key_params.name: rel
key_params.note: Interpret start/end as shifts from old start/end

key_params.name: cur
key_params.note: Interpret interval relative to current frame

common_gotchas: Stretch CHOP preserves the sample rate; it changes interval timing.
Use Resample CHOP when the sample rate itself must change.
Cubic interpolation can oversmooth or ring around sharp transitions.
Pulse Preserve is safer for trigger channels that must remain one-sample pulses.
Constant Area changes amplitude to preserve total area, which may be surprising for control signals.
Reverse Interval flips sample order after interval handling.
Stretch CHOP changes interval timing but not sample-rate metadata.
